questions.questionText: Which one of the following is most likely to influence the price elasticity of supply of a good or service?
options: The availability of spare capacity
The number of substitutes for the product
The percentage of income spent on the good
The price of complementary goods

questions.questionText: Figure 3 below shows the supply curve (S) for cakes. Which one of the following can be concluded from Figure 3? The supply of cakes
options: is less price inelastic when price increases from £8 to £10 than when it increases from £10 to £15.
is more price inelastic when price increases from £8 to £10 than when it increases from £10 to £15.
is price elastic when the price increases from £8 to £10 and when it increases from £10 to £15.
is unitary price elastic when price increases from £8 to £10 and when it increases from £10 to £15.

questions.questionText: Extract B (lines 3–4) states that ‘Universities have expanded the number of places on offer to students, but the supply of student accommodation is highly inelastic’. With the help of a diagram, explain the impact of the increase in the number of students attending university on the market for student accommodation.
The price of carrots falls from 60p to 54p per kilo. As a result of this fall in price, the quantity supplied falls by a quarter. What is the price elasticity of supply?

Figure 2 shows the demand (D) and supply (S) curves for diamonds. An increase in demand shifts the demand curve from D1 to D2. Using Figure 2, which one of the following is the price elasticity of supply for diamonds?

A government sets a maximum price for fruit below the market price to try to encourage healthier eating. All other things being equal, which one of the following will result in the lowest amount of excess demand for fruit at the maximum price?
options: Demand is income elastic and supply is price elastic.
Demand is income inelastic and supply is price inelastic.
Demand is price elastic and supply is price elastic.
Demand is price inelastic and supply is price inelastic.

questions.questionText: Explain possible reasons for fluctuations in the world market price of tea.

A fast food restaurant is willing to supply 3000 burgers a week at a market price of £5 a burger. The price elasticity of supply of burgers is 2. If the market price falls to £4 a burger, the number of burgers that the restaurant will be willing to supply will be
Which one of the following is a reason why the supply of cars is likely to be price elastic in the short run when the price of cars increases?
options: Car manufacturers’ stocks of unsold cars are low
The demand for cars is also price elastic
The marginal cost of producing cars increases significantly with output
There is considerable spare capacity in the car industry

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements about price elasticity of supply is correct? Price elasticity of supply
options: increases when a firm’s labour costs increase.
is affected by the amount of spare capacity.
measures the responsiveness of price to a change in supply.
tends to be lower in the long run than in the short run.

questions.questionText: A rise in the price of blueberries from £8 to £10 per kg encourages growers to increase their supply from 12 kg to 21 kg each week. Other things remaining the same, this suggests that the price elasticity of supply for blueberries is
The diagram below shows two market demand curves (D1 and D2) and the market supply curve (S), for Good X. The price elasticity of supply of Good X when the demand curve shifts from D1 to D2 is
Online clothes retailers invest in new warehouses to enable them to hold larger stocks of clothes. Other things remaining the same, this is most likely to result in
options: a higher price elasticity of supply of clothes sold online.
an increase in demand for clothes sold online.
diseconomies of scale in the online clothes industry.
lower barriers to entry to the online clothes industry.

questions.questionText: At the initial market equilibrium, the income elasticity of demand for fresh chickens is +1.5, and the price elasticity of supply is +1.0. Then there is a 5% increase in consumers’ income. Which one of the following combinations, A, B, C or D, is most likely to show the changes in the market equilibrium price and quantity?

The diagram below shows the original market demand (D1) and supply (S) curves for fresh strawberries. A decrease in the demand for fresh strawberries shifts the demand curve from D1 to D2. From the above diagram, it can be concluded that when the equilibrium price of fresh strawberries falls from £5 per kilo to £4 per kilo, the price elasticity of supply of strawberries is
Many agricultural products are subject to large fluctuations in price. One reason why these large fluctuations occur is because the
options: demand for agricultural products is income inelastic in the long run.
supply of agricultural products is price elastic in the long run.
supply of agricultural products is price inelastic in the short run.
demand for agricultural products is price elastic in the short run.

questions.questionText: A good has a price elasticity of supply of +0.8. At present, the quantity supplied of the good is 200 units per week at a market price of £800 per unit. If the price rises to £1000 per unit then the quantity supplied per week would
options: increase to 250 units.
increase to 240 units.
increase to 360 units.
decrease to 160 units.

questions.questionText: The elasticity of supply of a particular good is more likely to be low
options: the shorter the time period under consideration.
if the good in question has many close substitutes.
if the good in question is a necessity.
if complementary goods are required for its consumption.
